journey:dali-sacrament-of-the-last-suppe.t: The Sacrament of the Last Supper
journey:dali-sacrament-of-the-last-suppe.l: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C., USA
journey:dali-sacrament-of-the-last-suppe.noimg: © Salvador Dalí, Fundació Gala-Salvador Dalí / Artists Rights Society. View it on the National Gallery of Art website.

x.summary: Christ sits at a stone table before a calm bay, with twelve disciples bowed in prayer around him, while a vast transparent torso floats above with outstretched arms. The room is set within a huge, glass-like dodecahedron, a geometric figure that Plato associated with the cosmos. Dalí, who had returned to Catholicism, presents the Last Supper as a timeless, luminous sacrament rather than a dramatic meal.
facts: The landscape is the bay of Port Lligat, near Dalí's home on the Costa Brava.

The banker and collector Chester Dale, who had told Dalí he must paint 'one more religious picture', acquired it and placed it at the National Gallery, believing it 'too important to keep for a few'; it formally entered the collection with the Chester Dale Collection in 1963.
It became one of the most-viewed paintings at the National Gallery, even as critics debated its worth; the theologian Paul Tillich dismissed it as 'junk'.
